summary: Body mass across terrestrial mammals is open in PanTHERIA (5-1_AdultBodyMass_g) and PHYLACINE 1.2 (CC0, includes recently extinct megafauna). The Campione & Evans Dryad table pairs humeral/femoral midshaft circumference with body mass for extant terrestrial vertebrates, so the square-cube scaling of bone cross-section vs. mass can be examined; MorphoSource has thousands of limb-bone meshes (4,750 'femur' hits, 27 'Loxodonta') but without matched body mass. Nothing found supplies bone material strength, posture or performance, so a true safety-factor 'upper limit' remains uncompiled.
next_step: Pre-register a scaling test of stylopodial circumference vs. body mass on dryad.868mr (exponent vs. isometric 1/3), with mass ranges checked against PHYLACINE; a safety-factor test would need published bone-strength and posture values added by hand.
obstacles_confirmed: Bone meshes and body-mass tables are not linked individual by individual.
Safety factors need posture and duty factor, which mass and diameter do not contain.
